summary: @hubsync/web-sdk-react ships preinstall dropper that fetches Bun runtime to execute obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from oven-sh/bun GitHub releases (v1.3.13), extracts it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a sibling file `math_init.js` — a 727KB heavily obfuscated Bun-compiled bundle (string-array rotation via `WV8StW`, hex-named identifiers, large opcode array `n7gIxM`, `// @bun @bun-cjs` header) that ships without source, sourcemap, or documentation and is not referenced by the advertised React SDK API. The runtime download and payload execution fire automatically on `npm install`. The package name `@hubsync/web-sdk-react` is unrelated to the code it wraps: the `description` field, README, install instructions, and all documented URLs belong to Verdocs (`@verdocs/web-sdk-react`, `api.verdocs.com`, `developers.verdocs.com`), and the shipped `dist/` appears to be a copy of the legitimate Verdocs library with the preinstall dropper and `math_init.js` payload appended. Executing an opaque, obfuscated blob under an alternate runtime at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern; using Bun to execute the payload evades Node-based supply-chain scanners.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
